name: webchat
description: Leech onto your logged-in web AI chat (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Qwen…) and run a full agentic coding loop in your editor — no API keys, no metered tokens.

enumDescriptions: Ask: review a diff before applying edits, and approve any tool/command runs.
Auto-edit: apply file changes automatically, but still approve tool/command runs.
Plan: return a step-by-step plan only — no edits, no commands.
Full access: apply edits AND run tools/commands automatically, no approvals (destructive commands still ask unless webchat.agent.confirmDangerousCommands is off). Every change can be undone.
webchat.agent.mode.description: Agent mode. Controls whether LeechCode asks before applying edits and running tools. User-level only, so a repository's settings can't change it.

webchat.agent.maxToolIterations.description: How many tool rounds (read → edit → run → read…) the agent may do for one task before pausing. 0 = default (6, or 25 in full access).

webchat.agent.confirmDangerousCommands.description: In full access mode, still ask before running commands that look destructive: deleting a drive/home/parent folder, formatting disks, force-pushing, git reset --hard / clean -f, piping a downloaded script into a shell, sudo, shutdown.

webchat.prompt.includeSelectionOnly.description: Use only the current editor selection when building context.

webchat.context.maxIndexChars.description: Paste-safe character budget for @codebase / /index whole-workspace indexing. The file tree is always included; file contents fill up to this many characters. Larger values risk freezing the web chat input on paste.

webchat.context.maxTreeChars.description: Character budget for the compact PROJECT_STRUCTURE.txt file tree included with every prompt so the model always knows the repository layout (and can read_file what it needs).

webchat.provider.maxMessageChars.markdownDescription: Per-provider max characters for a single chat message, e.g. `{ "chatgpt": 12000, "qwen": 8000 }`. WebChat caps the built prompt's context to fit this so messages aren't rejected as "too long". Editable per provider from the in-panel Settings.

webchat.provider.models.markdownDescription: Per-provider model lists for the in-panel model switcher, e.g. `{ "gemini": ["3 Flash", "3 Pro"] }`. When set for a provider it fully replaces the built-in defaults — providers rename/deprecate models often, so add or remove entries from the in-panel Settings. Each entry should match (part of) the name shown in the provider's own model menu.

webchat.provider.maxSessionChars.markdownDescription: Per-provider total character budget for one chat conversation, e.g. `{ "chatgpt": 800000, "claude": 600000 }`. LeechCode starts a fresh chat when ~90% of it is used, and caps how much of a whole-codebase index it delivers. Editable per provider from the in-panel Settings.

webchat.index.chunked.description: When @codebase / /index is too large for one message, deliver it as several ordered messages (the chat acknowledges each) instead of truncating it to a single paste-safe message.

webchat.index.maxChunks.description: Safety cap on the number of messages used to deliver a chunked codebase index. Files beyond this many messages are skipped.

webchat.request.timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait without any feedback from the chat page before treating a request as failed (a closed tab or a stuck page would otherwise stall the task forever).

enumDescriptions: Off: a failed request is only reported; you retry or switch provider yourself.
Safe: hand the task to another provider automatically, but only when the failure happened before the provider saw the prompt (nothing can be duplicated).
Always: also offer to continue after an ambiguous failure (the provider may already have edited files or run commands) — LeechCode asks first.
webchat.failover.mode.markdownDescription: What to do when a request fails in the browser. A handover message is built locally (objective, files already changed, tool output, errors) because a provider's own chat history cannot be transferred.

webchat.failover.providers.markdownDescription: Ordered provider ids to try when failing over, e.g. `["chatgpt", "claude", "gemini"]`. Empty = the current provider first, then the rest.

webchat.customProviders.markdownDescription: Extra web AI chat sites to drive, beyond the built-ins. Only `label` and `url` are required — the browser extension finds the input/send button/reply automatically, and you can fix a site by right-clicking an element → **WebChat Bridge**. Add sites from ⚙ Settings → Custom AI sites.

id.description: Optional stable id (defaults to the hostname).

label.description: Name shown in the provider switcher.

url.description: Chat page URL, e.g. https://chat.z.ai/ (https only; http allowed for localhost).

inputSelector.description: Optional CSS selector for the message box.

submitSelector.description: Optional CSS selector for the Send button.

responseSelector.description: Optional CSS selector matching each assistant reply.

webchat.bridge.port.description: Localhost port used by the IDE-to-browser bridge.

webchat.bridge.token.markdownDescription: Advanced override for the bridge pairing token. Leave empty (recommended) to use the random per-install token kept in the OS keychain — copy it with **LeechCode: Copy Bridge Pairing Token**. Values shorter than 24 characters, or the old `webchat-dev-token`, are ignored.

webchat.browser.autoSubmit.description: Automatically submit prompts after inserting them into the web chat input.

webchat.agent.autoApplyFileChanges.description: Legacy fallback for applying validated WebChat agent file changes. Prefer webchat.agent.applyMode.

webchat.agent.applyMode.description: Controls whether WebChat asks, automatically applies, or never applies agent file changes.

webchat.diff.showOnApply.description: Open a before→after diff for each file WebChat applies, so you can see exactly what changed.

webchat.vision.enabled.description: Process attached/pasted images with your OWN local vision model instead of relying on the web chat's (limited) image support. The image's description/OCR is injected into the prompt as text.

webchat.vision.endpoint.markdownDescription: OpenAI-compatible chat-completions URL for local image analysis, e.g. Ollama `http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions` or LM Studio `http://localhost:1234/v1/chat/completions`.

webchat.vision.model.markdownDescription: Vision model name at the endpoint, e.g. `llava`, `llama3.2-vision`, `qwen2.5vl`, `minicpm-v`.

webchat.vision.apiKey.description: Optional bearer token for the vision endpoint (usually blank for local servers).

webchat.vision.prompt.default: Describe this image in detail and transcribe any visible text (OCR) exactly. Focus on anything relevant to a software/coding task (UI, code, errors, diagrams).
webchat.vision.prompt.description: Instruction sent to your local vision model for each image.

webchat.agent.autoRepairInvalidResponses.description: Ask the web chat for one corrected tool response when the returned agent JSON is malformed.

webchat.agent.maxRepairAttempts.description: Maximum automatic repair prompts to send for one malformed agent response.

webchat.session.maxContextTokens.description: Upper bound on the approximate token budget of one web chat before a fresh chat is started. Each provider's own conversation window (webchat.provider.maxSessionChars) caps it further.

webchat.session.maxInputTokens.description: Upper bound on the approximate input-token budget of one web chat (also capped by the provider's conversation window).

webchat.session.maxOutputTokens.description: Upper bound on the approximate output-token budget of one web chat (also capped by the provider's conversation window).

webchat.session.compactEveryPrompts.description: Every N user prompts, also ask the assistant for a thorough compacted development state (the prompt itself is still sent).

webchat.session.rotateWhenBudgetRemainin.description: Start a fresh web chat when remaining session budget falls below this ratio.
